The core operator is the meta-regressor that predicts error percentiles u_{i,t} = #{j∈T_i: j≠t, e_{i,j} < e_{i,t}} / (|T_i|+1) using lag-window features. This enables selective forecasting by defining a gate s(x) such that if u_{i,t} exceeds a threshold q, the forecast is withheld. The mathematical duality lies in treating error percentiles as posterior quantiles in Bayesian inference, where the meta-model acts as a surrogate likelihood estimator. Failure modes include overfitting in meta-training, poor generalization due to domain shift, and misalignment between feature representation and error structure. The system exhibits robustness through zero-shot transfer but requires domain adaptation for optimal performance. Risk-coverage curves provide empirical validation of the trade-off between coverage and risk, with AUCO measuring deviation from oracle efficiency.
